applicabilityBasis.summary: FIDD is a Fidelity-issued U.S. dollar payment stablecoin with 1:1 redemption and monthly reserve attestations, issued by a federally chartered OCC-supervised national trust bank.

genius.notes: Reviewed 2026-10-07. Fidelity Digital Assets, National Association is the sole FIDD issuer and USD redemption obligor. The OCC active trust-bank list as of August 31, 2026 names charter 25398; NYDFS records federal conversion effective December 12, 2025. The uninsured national trust-bank charter establishes existing OCC licensing, not a GENIUS section 5 approval or an announced GENIUS application. issuerPathway remains unknown and the GENIUS-specific primaryFederalRegulator field is omitted pending evidence of a current or announced GENIUS route. OCC decision conditions 3 and 5 distinguish future GENIUS compliance and a separate written stablecoin nonobjection from charter approval. The opened records and named searches found no qualifying public GENIUS approval, official application or GENIUS enforcement action for FIDD. This bounded negative finding does not establish the absence of confidential filings or unrelated historical actions. February 4 issuer launch commentary describes regulatory clarity without announcing a GENIUS application. The September 25, 2026 PwC examination covers August 7 and 31 reserves and does not examine legal or regulatory compliance. not-yet-restricted refers to GENIUS DASP timing, not a guarantee of availability in every jurisdiction.

negativeEvidenceReview.summary: The opened issuer and regulator sources and exact-name searches through 2026-10-07 did not locate a public FIDD/Fidelity Digital Assets, National Association GENIUS section 5 approval, state qualification, official GENIUS application or GENIUS enforcement action. The ordinary trust-bank charter and separate stablecoin activity nonobjection condition do not establish GENIUS authorization. Federal Register FIDD search returned no records; the issuer/GENIUS result was an SEC custody proposal citing bank charters, not an issuer authorization. Issuer launch commentary does not announce a GENIUS application. Findings are limited to the reviewed public record and do not rule out unpublished filings.
